questions.q: What are the four stages of a build-and-deploy pipeline for a Kubernetes application?
options: Build, push, update, roll out
Plan, apply, destroy, import
Commit, branch, merge, tag
Lint, format, compile, archive
questions.explain: Build turns source into an image, push uploads it to a registry, update points the manifest at the new tag, and roll out applies and confirms the change.

questions.q: Why does Northbridge Retail tag container images with the Git commit SHA instead of `latest`?
options: So the exact code running in production is always traceable back to one specific commit, and every build is distinguishable
Because Kubernetes refuses to pull any image tagged `latest`
Because commit SHAs make the image file smaller
It has no real benefit — either tag works identically
questions.explain: A unique, traceable tag like the commit SHA means you can always tell exactly which code is deployed, and two different builds never collide under the same tag.

questions.q: What does `kubectl set image` actually do?
options: Patches a Deployment's pod template with a new image reference, triggering Kubernetes' rolling update
Builds a new container image from source code
Deletes the Deployment and all its pods immediately
Pushes an image to a container registry
questions.explain: `kubectl set image` updates the Deployment spec, which Kubernetes then reconciles via a rolling update — starting new pods and retiring old ones once the new ones are healthy.

questions.q: Why does the pipeline run `kubectl rollout status` (or Helm's `--wait`) after triggering a deploy?
options: To block the job until every new pod is confirmed healthy, failing the build if the rollout stalls, instead of declaring success blindly
To print the cluster's total CPU usage
To delete old container images from the registry
It's optional and has no effect on whether the job passes or fails
questions.explain: Without this step, the pipeline would report success the moment it issued the update command, even if the new pods never actually became healthy.

questions.q: When does Northbridge Retail's pipeline reach for Helm instead of a raw `kubectl set image` command?
options: For services with more moving parts — multiple environments or templated configuration
Never — Helm is only used for local development, not CI/CD
Only when deploying to a cluster that has no readiness probes
Only on the very first deployment of any service, ever
questions.explain: Helm's templating and `--install`/`--wait` flags are more useful once a service has more configuration complexity than a single Deployment's image tag.
